newsitem.title: USA: IBM tumbles on renewed Q1 earnings fears.
newsitem.headline: IBM tumbles on renewed Q1 earnings fears.

text.p: Shares of International Business Machines Corp tumbled Thursday on renewed fears that currency translations and a mainframe product transition will hurt its first quarter earnings, analysts and traders said.
The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column today highlighted the actions about two weeks ago by a few analysts who cut their earnings estimates on IBM.

Analysts and traders said there were no new factors driving IBM down, other than renewed jitters about the first quarter. Some investors are nervous that IBM may miss the First Call consensus earnings estimate of $2.31 a share, they said.
IBM is expected to report first quarter earnings April 23.
On March 20-21, negative comments by analysts at Dean Witter, Morgan Stanley and Merrill Lynch fueled a drop in IBM's stock.

Jay Stevens of Dean Witter cut his first half earnings estimates by $0.10 a share and added $0.05 to his second half estimate, resulting in a net estimate cut of $0.05 for the year, to $12.25 a share. He said more revenues were expected in the second half as customers delay purchases of mainframes until an upgrade comes in June.
Steve Milunovich of Morgan Stanley also cut IBM estimates.
Daniel Mandresh of Merrill Lynch warned clients of a tough comparison versus the year-ago first quarter, saying he expects a $0.20-a-share hit to earnings due to currency.

Traders said they did not believe a rumor that began surfacing a week and a half ago that IBM would pre-announce an earnings shortfall. "I heard the rumor but I wouldn't put any credence to it," said one technology trader.

Gary Helmig, a SoundView Financial analyst, said IBM has pre-announced an earnings shortfall only twice in its recent history. Helmig has not changed his first quarter earnings estimate of $2.32 a share, which he has had since February.
"It's going to be tough to make that number and I doubt that they can over-achieve it," Helmig said.
He added that foreign currency exchange rates have not changed drastically since February, so he sees nothing new to impact his estimate.
Traders and analysts said they had not heard of any new earnings estimate cuts that might have led to the drop in IBM shares.
"The Wall Street Journal article today is a summation of old news," said John Jones of Salomon Brothers. "We talked to IBM today and they have no plans for a pre-announcement."
One trader said of the newspaper article, "They are a bit late to the party here."
